intro: Patagonia is a small town in the grasslands of southern Arizona, in Santa Cruz County between the Santa Rita and Patagonia mountains, a short drive from the Mexican border. On an empty lot on North 4th Street grows a mesquite a reader calls enormous: about 14 metres tall and 18 metres across by their figures, its dark shaggy trunk breaking into a crowd of crooked limbs. A reader sent us its photograph.

question_answer: The tree to see in Patagonia, Arizona is the old mesquite on an empty lot at 200 North 4th Street, about 14 metres tall and 18 metres across by the figures of the reader who sent it. Its age is not known.
question_context: A reader sent us this mesquite from Patagonia, a small town in Santa Cruz County, southern Arizona, and called it an enormous, gnarly old tree on a town lot that is currently undeveloped. Their photograph looks straight up from the foot of the trunk: dark, shaggy bark broken into long plates, and a short trunk that splits into a crowd of heavy limbs wandering in every direction, several sawn off long ago and grown round at the cuts, under a fine web of feathery leaves. By their figures it is about 14 metres tall, 18 metres across and 300 centimetres round. Those are the reader's figures, not a measurement we have seen, and nobody has told us its age. Mesquites are more often shrubs or small trees, which is why one of this size stands out. The lot is private, so the way to see the tree is from North 4th Street.

trees.story:
"Enormous gnarly old mesquite on town lot, currently undeveloped," is how a reader described this tree when they sent it to us from Patagonia, a small town in the grasslands of southern Arizona. It stands on an empty lot on North 4th Street.

Their photograph looks straight up from the foot of the trunk, and gnarly is the word. The bark is dark and shaggy, broken into long rough plates. The trunk heaves itself up and splits into a whole crowd of heavy limbs that wander off in every direction, several of them sawn off short years ago and grown round at the cuts. Above them a fine web of twigs carries the small, feathery leaves of a mesquite against a pale sky.

By the reader's figures it is about 14 metres tall, 18 metres across and 300 centimetres round. Those figures are theirs; we have not seen a measurement, and we do not know its age. Mesquites are more often shrubs or small trees, so one of this size stands out. Which mesquite it is we would also like a reader to tell us.

The lot is private ground, so look from the street. If you know this tree's history, tell us here.
